references.text: Direct quote from [ref:Sal 110:1|Psalm 110:1], where David himself writes: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet." Jesus quotes this verse to show that the Messiah is more than just David's son—David himself calls him "Lord".
Parallel passage in [ref:Matt 22:43-45|Matthew 22:43-45], where Jesus asks the Pharisees the same question about how David, in the Spirit, can call the Messiah "Lord" if he is only David's son.
Parallel passage in [ref:Mark 12:36-37|Mark 12:36-37], where Jesus quotes Psalm 110:1 in the temple and points out that David himself calls him Lord.

Peter quotes the same verse from [ref:Apg 2:34-35|Acts 2:34-35] in his Pentecost sermon to prove that Jesus has been exalted to God's right hand, and that David was not speaking about himself but about Christ.
[ref:Hebr 1:13|Hebrews 1:13] quotes Psalm 110:1 to show that the Son is exalted above the angels, and that God never said to any angel: "Sit at my right hand".
[ref:Hebr 10:12-13|Hebrews 10:12-13] refers to Psalm 110:1 and describes Christ sitting at God's right hand, waiting until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.
[ref:1 Kor 15:25|1 Corinthians 15:25] alludes to Psalm 110:1 when Paul writes that Christ must reign until God has put all his enemies under his feet.
